title.narrative: UN Women Transformative Approaches to Achieving GE in Ukraine Fas II 2022-2026
UN Women Transformative Approaches to Achieving GE in Ukraine Phase II 2022-2026

description.narrative:
Insatsen syftar till att bidra till transformativa tillvägagångssätt för att bidra till ökad jämställdhet och kvinnorss egenmakt genom att fokusera på de hinder som kvinnor möter.
Genom att arbeta på ett holistiskt sätt med en bred grupp av aktörer (lokala och nationella institutioner, civila samhället och näringslivet) ämnar man bidra till ökat genomslag och genomförande samt implementering av internationella och nationella åtaganden rörande kvinnors rättigheter och jämställdhet och öven bidra till förbättrad dialog mellan parterna.

The project aims to employ transformative approaches to the advancement of gender equality and women’s empowerment by focusing on barriers that women face and empowering women through working with women, gender-transformative approaches engage a variety of agents of change. Transformative approaches aim at removing the root causes, structural barriers and restrictive social norms that underpin the persistence of gender inequalities in various areas of life. In the case of the proposed project, a transformative approach means engaging with the key institutions at the same time, specifically those that either have a significant impact on the replication of restrictive gender stereotypes or can help break down these social norms and pave the way for greater gender equality and women’s empowerment. The project builds on involving the three below specified groups of actors to acheive the proposed objectives described in the project proposal. 1) Key national- level institutions that will develop, implement, monitor and coordinate Ukraine´s international and national commitments to gender equality and women´s empowerment (here abbreviated GEWE) 2) Women and women´s organisations, that will participate in decision-making, monitoring of governmental commitments and advocacy for GEWE priorities 3) Private business companies - who will contribute to advancing GEWE in the workplace, value chains and in communities. By involving these actors, all in their specific responsibility, right as well as competence, the project aims at bringing about systemic change in the preconditions setting limitations for womens full participation and enjoyment of equal rights. The project strategy is that by involving the above mentioned key stakeholders the implementation of international standards and national GEWE commitments will be well coordinated, financed, and monitored in partnership thus strenghtening joint accountability to contribute to transformative changes to improve the lives of women and girls in Ukraine.

The project goal, that the Government, civil society and the private sector have joint accountability to contribute towards transformative results for gender equality and women's empowerment in Ukraine, will be achieved under three Outcomes and five Outputs:
OUTCOME 1 Key national-level institutions develop, implement, monitor and coordinate Ukraine's international and national commitments to GEWE.
OUTPUT 1.1 Key institutions of the National Women's Machinery (NWM) have strengthened capacities to implement their respective GEWE mandates. OUTPUT 1.2 The national-level GEWE Coordination Mechanism is strengthened to be fully operational, participatory and inclusive.
OUTCOME 2 Women and women's organizations meaningfully participate in evidence-based decision-making, monitoring of governmental commitments and advocacy for GEWE priorities.
OUTPUT 2.1 Women and women's organizations have improved capacities to participate in the development and monitoring of the Governments GEWE commitments. OUTPUT 2.2 Women's rights activists increasingly collaborate with the media to challenge patriarchal social norms and advocate for their priorities.
OUTCOME 3 Private business companies contribute to advancing GEWE in the workplace, in value chains and in communities.
OUTPUT 3.1 Private business companies have strengthened knowledge, plans and mechanisms in place to implement the Women's Empowerment Principles.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution UN Women Ukraine

description.narrative:
The project is assessed to have strengthened joint accountability of the government, the civil society and the private sector in advancing gender equality in Ukraine over the years 2022-2025.
Key results include:
- Legal and policy achievement with 23 new and revised laws and national policy advancing gender equality, such as the Istanbul convention on combating violence against women, legislation on response to conflict related sexual violence, a state strategy and action plan on equal rights and opportunities for women and men until 2030 as well as a third national action plan on UN Security Council Resolution (UNSCR) 1325 on women, peace and security (WPS) until 2030 (NAP 1325).
- In 2025, gender-responsive budgeting (GRB) was institutionalized through amendments to the Budget Code for the first time in Ukraine's history. Building on this momentum, the National Employment Strategy until 2030, adopted in January 2026, explicitly recognizes women as a priority group in Ukraine's labour market, embedding targeted measures to address caregiving burdens, gender stereotypes in professional orientation, and the persistent gender pay gap within an EU-aligned framework, reflecting the sustained impact of the Project's policy advocacy well beyond its formal conclusion.
- Institutional capacity was strengthened systematically and sustainably across 15 National Women's Machinery institutions and relevant line ministries, with 13 partner governmental authorities meeting annual milestone targets for improved implementation and monitoring.
- A nationwide civil service training system on gender-equality related issues, developed in partnership with the National Agency on Civil Service (NACS) and the High School of Public Governance, certified 1,850 public servants across all oblasts of Ukraine, with a further 7,927 completing online courses on sexual harassment prevention and CRSV (conflict-related sexual violence) response developed under officially approved state curricula. A particularly significant sustainability milestone was reached in 2025, when 74 of the 119 certified trainers in the nationwide Training-of-Trainers network were certified that year alone, ensuring continued scaling of gender equality competencies across government institutions independently of project funding and using state budget resources.
- Coordination mechanisms were transformed from consultation forums into operational policy platforms, generating 21 joint actions and commitments on advancing gender equality. The Alliance for Gender-Responsive and Inclusive Recovery, co-established by UN Women, Ukraine, and Germany at the Ukrarine Recovery Conference in Berlin 2024, grew to more than 100 partners by the beginning of 2026, including 40 new members joining it in 2025, embedding gender equality in international financing and reconstruction decisions at scale.
- Women's rights advocates and civil society organizations moved from the margins to the centre of Ukraine's gender equality reform processes. Their direct contributions shaped 15 national GEWE documents, including laws and strategies on CRSV, GBV (gender-based violence) prevention, equal pay, regional development, and demographic policy. CSOs such as JurFem, LaStrada-Ukraine, and UAExperts provided expert input into Istanbul Convention alignment, while women's groups contributed to the Gender Pay Gap Strategy, the Regional Development Strategy, and the Law on Equal Rights and Opportunities. The Ukrainian Women Veterans Movement influenced the development of the Concept of a New Veteran Policy through direct engagement with the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Social Policy, and parliamentary committees.
- The private sector was mobilsed to advance gender equality in Ukraine. The Project played a catalytic role in building structured cooperation between businesses, government institutions, and civil society on gender equality. The Women's Empowerment Principles (WEPs) community in Ukraine grew to 62 signatory companies by the end of 2025, representing a critical mass of corporate leaders committed to gender equality in the workplace, supply chains, and communities. Between 2022 and 2025, private sector partners implemented 50 flagship initiatives integrating gender equality into workplace policies, corporate culture, and business ecosystems, with 22 companies developing structured WEPs Plans based on gender gap analysis. These commitments translated into concrete workplace reforms implemented by the private business: companies such as Aurora introduced family-friendly policies including childcare facilities and GBV support hotlines; DTEK, Ferrexpo, and Lika Comfort implemented reskilling programmes enabling women to enter technical and industrial occupations; and Ukrenergo, Projector, and The WEPs Award 2025 finalists - Lika Komfort, Intellias, and Avrora. Photo: UN Women/Serhii Piriiev Uklon launched employment and mentorship initiatives specifically targeting women veterans and families of military personnel. Through technical assistance and cooperation with WEP's companies, 459 women small-business owners strengthened their entrepreneurial capacities and accessed new market opportunities.
- Direct support to war-affected women combined individual empowerment with structural private sector engagement. The Women for the Future initiative reached 74,430 women through career development training, including 5,969 women through targeted mentoring programmes and a nationwide visibility campaign. Of 466 women who received individual mentoring supported by 126 private companies and 124 mentors, 22% secured new employment and 12% launched their own businesses.
- The project shifted to include humanitarian support in 2022-2023 to address the more urgent needs following the full-scale invasion, while maintaining its focus on long-term recovery. Through four women-led CSO partners, more than 3,500 war-affected women and girls, including women living near the front line and in de-occupied territories, internally displaced women, refugees, activists, volunteers, and their family members, received critical support spanning emergency humanitarian assistance, legal aid, psychosocial services, and economic empowerment.
- Changes among key actors:
At the governance level, the project contributed to a stronger, EU-aligned legislative and policy framework that expands women's rights, strengthens protection from gender-based and conflict-related sexual violence, and embeds gender equality into recovery, budgeting, and public accountability systems. Project`s interventions has improved the ability of national institutions to plan, implement, monitor, and publicly report on gender equality commitments, making gender equality a core part of Ukraine's reforms and accession architecture rather than a standalone agenda.
At the civil society level, the project strengthened women's organizations and women leaders to move from consultation to influence. Women's rights advocates increasingly contributed evidence, shaped national and local policies, monitored government commitments, and led public advocacy initiatives. This helped ensure that recovery and reform processes better reflected the needs and priorities of women and girls, including those most affected by war.
At the private sector level, the project helped establish a stronger ecosystem for women's economic empowerment by engaging the private sector as a partner in change. Companies increasingly adopted gender-responsive workplace policies, invested in women's leadership and skills development, and created opportunities for women entrepreneurs through mentoring, supplier linkages, and market access. This contributed to more inclusive workplaces, stronger support for war-affected women, and improved prospects for women's participation in economic recovery.
